page.layout: One printed page: running text in a single column, page number 47 at the head centre; a narrow strip of marginal notes in the left margin, cut off by the binding; a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: policiti. Resp Neutiquâ . sed exstitit noftro feculo novû hominû genus, qui politici videri volunt, & interea vitâ & moribus fese atheos probant. Hi magistratus, regum, ac principû edicta proferunt, quibus omni ex parte satisfaciendû judicât. Verûm ne interea oblivisçamur edictorum summi magistratus, Dei & Domini noftri Jesu Christi. Scimus,noftrum officium esse,honorificentissimè de magistratu sentire,tanquam de Dei ministris ac legatis,quantum ipsûm ordinem attinet ; fatemur, illorum mandatis esse parendum : Imò etiam malos principes ac tyrannicè dominantes eadem ratione reverebimur , quâ optimum regem, quantum ad publicam,obedientiam attinet.Parebimus ergo illis ex animo, sed usq; ad aras, ut ajunt,neâ Dei obedientiâ nos abducant. iniquum enim est, ut hominibus satisfacias, in ejus offensionem incurrere, propter quem hominib. ipsis obedias. Adversus Deum ergo[illegible, ~8 letters] si quid

page.notes: The left margin strip is cut off by the binding and only partly legible: its lines are printed in very small type and could not be read reliably, so the marginal notes are marked as illegible rather than guessed. The visible fragments are roughly "qui turbabat", "gebatur crimen", "Dei", "multum", "rerum", "omnia", "gravitèr", "obedientiam" and similar; none can be confirmed letter by letter, so I have not transcribed them. The line "policiti." is italic and is the end of a word that began on the previous page ("politici"); the catchword "si quid" is set at the right below the last full line. Words marked with a long s-like letter are transcribed as plain s; "ajunt" and "neâ" follow the printed spelling.
